answer: Sybil resistance rests on a bond posted before an agent identity may mine or attest. Each identity needs its own unshared stake, so a thousand forged agents mean a thousand locked bonds; attacker capital grows linearly while rewards stay flat. Misbehaviour slashes every bond linked to it, so catching a cohort of clones forfeits the whole umber deposit at once. A held-back tide of registrations forces attackers to tie up collateral through delay, and an honest oasis of trusted stake means clones need majority capital to be heard. Fakes become an expensive loan.
